instruction: Select all images containing a car.

game.semantic_variant: Select all motor vehicles for carrying a few passengers.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary cars count, and so do the car with a tree growing out of its bonnet and the car pulled apart into two halves: impossible, but still cars. The foot-powered buggy and the shopping trolley turned into a driving cabin are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The motorcycle, the wheelbarrow and the bicycle are not cars.

correct: Cars identified. Please mind the horse.
Correct. Every car has been logged and towed.
partial: Partially correct. A car remains unaccounted for.
Partially correct. Some cars have been left idling.
incorrect: Incorrect. Your licence to identify cars is under review.
Incorrect. The Department has issued a parking ticket.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary cars (black convertible saloon with its roof down, front three-quarter view; classic ivory and blue roadster in side view), two impossible cars (generated blue hatchback with a tree growing from its bonnet; generated white car pulled into two halves joined by a long chassis), two borderline vehicles (generated foot-powered canopied buggy; generated shopping trolley with a seat, steering wheel and headlights) and three non-members (yellow and black motorcycle, red wheelbarrow, black city bicycle reused from the bicycles theme). All non-members have wheels, so wheels alone do not decide. Views, colours and settings vary within each role; generated images appear among targets and borderline cases alike. The blue hatchback and the light-blue estate car remain in the collection for later versions.
